title: Is This Game Any Good ?
author: Patient-Sprinkles920
selftext: This is my first 2D game. I used Claude to write the code and Grok to generate the art. I spent 6-9 months working on it in my spare time. Now I really tried to keep adding juice to it until it felt fun and addictive. I think I achieved that but so far since launch (Google Play) there have been very few downloads. Is the game or my lack of marketing or both the problem. The game was developed on a Samsung Android tablet and plays best on Android tablets. I honestly think the PC version looks king of bad. I would love honest opinions as I am trying to get better. Here is the link if interested: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.oceanstudios.blazesoceanquest&pcampaignid=web\_share](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.oceanstudios.blazesoceanquest&pcampaignid=web_share)

comments.author: frankenstein-0x00e
comments.body:
I think its held back by the promo art

I respect people's decisions to use image gen (i dont like it personally) but here is an advice 

Take those images you generated as material for your game, take screenshot of how it looks in the store, send it to claude (ideally because claude generally has better taste than chatgpt)   
and ask it to make it into store page material (playstore) and it will figure out resolutions, makes  you a better icon, or even edits a better montage for your game. Then some marketing 



Another thing is I advise you to study some game dev stuff such as gamefeel, and ask yourself does this action provide me with the expected joy? try the game with sound on and off, does sound do its job or is it there for the sake of sound? are the animations on the same style or each object having different animation speed



these are all things even a toddler can subconsciously feel while playing your game but can't name. its what makes a game addictive to try and provide fun to the subconsciousness of the player 

  
It's a good game you made but I am pretty sure it won't be your best because you will only get better! good job

replies.author: frankenstein-0x00e
replies.body:
for the icon try a close up shot with a stylish perspect, a fish with less colors (meaning a RED fish with blue EYES or something, LESSER DETAILS , and add a word or something next to it

Max the heck out of vibrance (Also try shaders on your game , at least some layers they do wonders, if u dont know what they are go learn them , they make or break a game's aesthetic!!!)



Dont try to reinvent the wheel, learn from references if you look at these icons for examples, you see how less clutter and how zoomed in they feel? mainly just the face to hook your eye either by being the center or by being the biggest object in the image , less details more basic shapes, maxed out saturation/ vibrance or whatever the heck does the colorfulness

  
AI GAME dev is all about KNOWING that something exists, if u dont know that CERTAIN Aesthetic or practice or mechanic or whatever EXISTS you can't ask AI to make it, and AI will try to satisfy you by simply saying nothing and doing what u ask   
SO YOU break that cycle by ASKING IT "what do you think feels wrong here? criticize it effectively"  

  
(just trigger warning, you will be destroyed by the AI's critic side)

replies.author: Patient-Sprinkles920
replies.body: I like the "study what exists" advice..  find what I like and why is a great way to get better. and I agree on asking AI to be critical, it defaults to overly agreeable, every idea is fantastic, blah, blah,. Oh, and I have moved my art creation to blender for the current game I am working on..  Much better consistency that way.

replies.author: Patient-Sprinkles920
replies.body: Thank you sir !  All good advice. I do know the animation /art styles don't all jive perfectly. The bubble varieties is where I tried to get most of the fun factor from.
